chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Husayn al-Ahmasi, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
No, by Allah! No servant would insist upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, except that Allah would answer him.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for persisting in supplication to Allah?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him) affirms that persistent insistence (ilhāḥ) in supplication guarantees a response, highlighting the spiritual discipline of not giving up even when the answer seems delayed. This concept is central to Shia devotional practice, where 'awaiting the answer' (intizār al-faraj) is viewed as a form of worship that strengthens the bond between the servant and the Creator. The hadith underscores that Allah’s promise to respond is absolute, though the form and timing of the response may vary according to divine wisdom.
